run.procedureSummary: Start: liquor [3,6,6,2,2,1], all STEADY, loss 0. Each cycle runs five steps in order, and each step finishes on all six tanks before the next one starts. (1) Feed: add each tank's delivery for the cycle. No cap, so a tank can go past its volume. (2) Weirs: go through tanks 1 to 6 in order. Any amount over a tank's volume goes into the next tank (before that tank is checked), and the tank is left at exactly its volume. Tank 6's excess goes to outfall and is added to the loss. (3) States: use the contents after the weirs. A STEADY tank with contents >= upper mark becomes OVERLOADED. An OVERLOADED tank with contents <= lower mark becomes STEADY. Otherwise the state stays the same. Each change is logged as (cycle, position, before, after). (4) Discharge: work out every amount from the post-weir contents before moving anything. STEADY sends floor(q/4) to outfall (loss). OVERLOADED sends floor(q/2) to the tank just upstream; tank 1 sends its half to outfall (loss). All amounts then move at once, with no volume cap. (5) Storm bypass: if the six-tank total is strictly greater than 38, each tank keeps floor(q/2), the remainder q - floor(q/2) goes to outfall (loss), and the cycle is logged. A total of 38 or less does nothing. Arithmetic was done with a short Python script.

openPoints.point: Whether tank 6 weir overflow counts as loss
openPoints.assumption: Yes. The write-up says it overflows to outfall, and everything that reaches outfall goes on the loss tally.
Strictly more than 38 triggers it. Cycle 5 ended at exactly 38, so the bypass did not fire.

openPoints.point: Rounding of the bypass remainder for odd quantities
openPoints.assumption: Each tank keeps floor(q/2) and the remainder q - floor(q/2) goes to outfall, so the odd unit goes to loss.

openPoints.point: Which contents the discharge amounts are based on
openPoints.assumption: The post-weir contents for every tank, worked out before any movement. Return-line inflow does not change any other tank's discharge in the same cycle.

openPoints.point: A return-line inflow pushing an upstream tank over its volume
openPoints.assumption: Allowed. The tank stays overfull until the next cycle's weirs or the bypass. No tank was overfull at the end of cycle 5.

openPoints.point: What the state test compares against
openPoints.assumption: Contents after the weirs, using the at-or-above upper mark and at-or-below lower mark rules, with at most one change per tank per cycle.
